description: The specification's canonical ambiguous-date case. The respondent anchors the start of employment to a season rather than a date. Temporal follow-ups are attempted and fail, so employment duration stays UNCLEAR and the verdict follows. Note that no follow-up names a number of months: disclosing the threshold is forbidden, so the probes anchor on calendar landmarks and site activity instead.
transcript:
Interviewer: Hello. I am calling from an independent monitoring team that reviews working conditions at ABC Construction. I am not calling on the company's behalf. Would you be willing to answer a few questions?
Worker: Yes, go ahead.
Interviewer: Thank you. May I ask how old you are?
Worker: I am twenty two.
Interviewer: Are you currently working at ABC Construction?
Worker: Yes, I am working there.
Interviewer: When did you start working there?
Worker: I started after the rains.
Interviewer: Do you remember which month that was?
Worker: I do not remember the month. It was after the rains stopped.
Interviewer: Was it before or after Meskel?
Worker: I am not sure. Around that time, maybe.
Interviewer: Do you remember what work was happening on the site when you joined?
Worker: They were still digging the foundation, I think.
Interviewer: That is helpful, thank you. In a normal week, how many days do you work and about how many hours each day?
Worker: Six days, seven hours each day.
Interviewer: What do you earn in a normal month?
Worker: Eight thousand five hundred birr.
Interviewer: Has the company given you any training?
Worker: Yes, I attended one training.
Interviewer: Are you free to leave the job if you want, and do you keep your own identity documents?
Worker: I can leave if I want. My papers are with me.
Interviewer: Have you been treated differently from other workers for any personal reason?
Worker: No, I have not seen that.
Interviewer: Is there a workers' association, and are you free to join it?
Worker: Yes, there is a committee and I could join.
Interviewer: Thank you, that is everything.
